title: Seasonal tidal-range change was uncertain at five Mid-Atlantic gauges between 1980-1999 and 2000-2020
abstract: We tested whether seasonal tide height changed with the larger seasonal mean sea-level contrast at five fixed Mid-Atlantic gauges. We used NOAA monthly records and compared September minus February in 2000-2020 with 1980-1999. The equal-site change in great diurnal range was -12.47 mm. Its 95% three-year block limits were -23.59 to -1.13 mm. One-year limits were -25.38 to +1.46 mm. Requiring the same years at all five sites gave -12.80 mm, with three-year limits of -26.84 to +1.92 mm. Thus, a regional range decrease was not clear across the planned checks. Mean sea-level contrast rose by 103.57 mm; higher high water rose by 93.86 mm and lower low water by 106.33 mm on the same records. The added higher-high-water offset fell by 9.71 mm, a secondary result. These are observed tide means, not predicted tides. The test does not identify a cause, tidal harmonic change, flood frequency, or storm change. Missing years, five selected sites, source errors, slow variability and conditional resampling limit inference. Code, paired contrasts, aggregate results, draws, source hashes and independent arithmetic checks support reproduction.

display.caption: Changes in September-minus-February levels and ranges. Intervals use joint three-year blocks. Common-year and one-year checks include zero for the primary regional great-range change.
